## Answer (based on the Office of Kaiju Affairs website)

**Yes — you are eligible to file this claim**, on the **Damage Compensation** page findings:

- Tanaka Bakery is 300 m inside the **Zone 4** corridor, and compensation covers zones 3, 4 and 5 (`/claims/damage-compensation/`, `/claims/eligibility/`).
- The damage is **verified structural damage** (shopfront and rear wall), and the incident occurred **21 days ago** — well inside the mandatory **90‑day filing window** (`/claims/eligibility/`, `/claims/how-to-file/`).
- No insurer has paid out, so there is no offset to apply — you can claim the full assessed award (had an insurer paid, the award would simply be reduced, not disqualified, per `/claims/eligibility/`).

### Extra support you qualify for

1. **Hardship supplement** — your household income (¥3,600,000) is below the ¥4,000,000 threshold, so you qualify automatically for the hardship supplement (`/claims/eligibility/`). You must submit a **household income certificate** to claim it.
2. **Assessment‑fee waiver** — the FAQ (`/claims/faq/`) states that claimants with **two or more approved claims from separate incidents within a rolling 12‑month period** are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee. Since your two earlier claims were approved within the last 12 months, this waiver applies automatically at lodgement — no separate application needed, and you should not have to pay the ¥12,000 fee.
3. **Business interruption compensation** — because Tanaka Bakery is a commercial property, you can also claim for business interruption in addition to structural damage, provided you include a **business registration certificate** (`/claims/damage-compensation/`, `/claims/how-to-file/`).

### Documents to bring when you lodge the claim

Per **"How to file a claim"** (`/claims/how-to-file/`) and the eligibility/FAQ pages, bring:

1. **Incident report receipt** — proof you filed the incident report within 72 hours of the event.
2. **Damage survey** — photographs and an itemised loss schedule documenting the structural damage to the shopfront and rear wall.
3. **Proof of ownership** of the property (as the bakery owner, since structural damage claims must be made by the owner).
4. **Business registration certificate** — required because you're claiming business‑interruption compensation for a commercial property.
5. **Household income certificate** — required to receive the hardship supplement.

You do **not** need an insurance settlement letter (no payout received), and thanks to the fee waiver you should not need to pay the ¥12,000 assessment fee at lodgement — though bring proof of your two prior approved claims in case the office needs to confirm the waiver.

All of this must be lodged within the 90‑day window (day 21 now, so you have time), after which an assessor visit will occur within 15 business days and a determination within 45 days of lodgement.

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Each one existed because a check had already scored an answer wrongly, and the last of them changed a finding that had already been handed over. They are listed so a reader can judge the instrument, including its history.

Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
